dialect.detail: Student lab exercise likely compiled with GnuCOBOL or similar academic COBOL environment; uses LINE SEQUENTIAL and ASSIGN TO PRINTER syntax common in GnuCOBOL/ACU-style environments

purpose.domain_detail: University COBOL programming course lab assignment on multi-level control breaks and arrays
purpose.summary: Reads a student input file containing department code, class code, student name, and 4 test scores. Performs a two-level control break (department as major, class as minor), calculates test averages, assigns letter grades, and prints a grouped summary report with class and department totals.

notable_features: EVALUATE TRUE for multi-level control break logic
OCCURS 4 TIMES array for test scores (input and output)
PERFORM VARYING loop to traverse array
Nested IF-ELSE chain for letter grade assignment (author notes it disturbs them)
ACCEPT FROM DATE for current date
Two-level control break: department (major) and class (minor)
verdict.notes: Filename and PROGRAM-ID confirm this is a student lab (LAB7MULTIBREAK). Author name (AUSTIN OGLETREE) is present. Comments include instructor instructions and a humorous self-comment about the nested IF block. No COMP-3, no SQL, no CICS. The VALUES (plural) keyword on a FILLER PIC X(5) is a minor syntax error that some compilers tolerate. Dialect is uncertain between GnuCOBOL and Micro Focus; LINE SEQUENTIAL and ASSIGN TO PRINTER are common in both academic environments.
